sections.h2: What builds up on Archer homes
body: Rural lots collect a particular mix of grime. Wind carries sand and field dust onto siding and screens. Rain splashes soil up the bottom two or three courses. Where sprinklers or shade keep a wall damp, mildew and algae take hold, especially on north walls, porch ceilings, and under deep ranch-house eaves. Concrete drives and walks pick up green film and tire marks.

None of that is just cosmetic. Mildew left on painted siding keeps the surface damp and eats into the film, which is why our pressure washing in Archer, FL is about protecting the coating as much as making the house look clean.

Different surfaces need different force. Too much pressure on painted siding can gouge wood, strip sound paint, and drive water behind laps and into wall cavities. Too little on concrete leaves stains behind.
bullets: Soft wash for painted siding, trim, soffits, screens, and roofs: low pressure with a cleaning solution that kills mildew at the root
Pressure wash for concrete driveways, walks, and pavers where the surface can take it
Hand detail for windows, light fixtures, and areas near plantings

body: Every exterior repaint we do starts with a wash and mildew treatment, because paint applied over a living film fails from underneath. If you are planning an exterior repaint in Archer, washing is already part of that estimate. If the paint is still sound and just dirty, a stand-alone soft wash can extend its life, and the crew lead will tell you honestly which one you need.
For background on what is growing on your walls, read our guide to mold and mildew on siding. Spring pollen also leaves yellow residue on porches and screens; our pollen stain article covers that.

Before washing, we wet down and cover nearby landscaping, close windows and doors, and plan runoff so cleaning solution does not pool near gardens or animal areas. Rinse is thorough. Decks and fences can be cleaned in the same visit; if they need refinishing afterward, see deck staining in Archer.

Screened porches are a common Archer request. Screens and frames collect dust and pollen fast, and a low-pressure wash cleans them without tearing the mesh. Porch ceilings, which often stay damp and grow mildew, get the same gentle treatment before any repaint.

faqs.q: Will soft washing damage my siding or paint?
faqs.a: No. Soft washing uses low pressure and a cleaning solution to kill mildew, so it cleans without stripping sound paint or forcing water behind siding.

faqs.q: Can you clean my concrete driveway too?
faqs.a: Yes. Concrete drives, walks, and pavers are pressure washed at higher pressure, which those surfaces can handle.

faqs.q: Do I need to wash before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Washing and mildew treatment are part of every exterior repaint we do, so it is already included when you book a paint job.
